parole.testo: Ultimately borrowed from Old French privilege, from Latin privilegium (“an ordinance or law against or in favor of an individual”), from privus (“private”) + lēx, legis (“law”).

Internationalism. Borrowing from any of a number of European languages, but ultimately from Old French parc (“livestock pen”), from Medieval Latin parcus, parricus, from Proto-Germanic *parrukaz (“enclosure, fence”).

From Old French catalogue, from Late Latin catalogus, itself from Ancient Greek κατάλογος (katálogos, “enrollment, register”), from καταλέγω (katalégō, “to recount, make a list”), from κατα- (kata-, “downwards, towards”) + λέγω (légō, “to say, to speak, to tell”). By surface analysis, ־לוֹג (-log).
